short: Gustavus Adolphus forced a crossing of the River Lech and defeated the Catholic League, mortally wounding their commander Tilly.
full:
On 15 April 1632, the Swedish army under Gustavus Adolphus executed a difficult contested river crossing over the Lech near Rain. Opposing them was the veteran Catholic League army commanded by Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly, who had entrenched his forces to block the Swedish advance into Bavaria.

Gustavus utilized intense artillery fire and smoke screens to cover the construction of a pontoon bridge. During the ensuing artillery duel, Tilly was struck in the leg by a cannonball and died weeks later. Deprived of their commander, the Catholic forces retreated, leaving Bavaria open to devastating Swedish occupation and removing one of the Empire's most capable generals.
